def test_large_values():
    """Test with large input values that cause overflow if max subtraction is omitted."""
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    # Scale large enough that raw values exceed ~710 (exp overflow in float64)
    x = torch.randn(4, 4, dtype=torch.float32) * 1e4   # typical values ~ few thousand
    y = softmax(x)
    y_ref = torch.softmax(x, dim=1)
    # The original kernel (with max subtraction) should match the reference;
    # the mutant (without subtraction) will produce Inf/NaN and fail this assert.
    assert torch.allclose(y, y_ref, atol=1e-5), (
        f"softmax mismatch on large values: max abs diff = {(y - y_ref).abs().max().item()}"
    )

# Append the new test after the existing sanity checks
test_large_values()

# Additional test that distinguishes the mutant (fp16 accumulator) from the original (fp32 accumulator)
M, N, K = 64, 64, 1024          # problem size well under the 2M-element limit
torch.manual_seed(123)          # deterministic input
a = torch.randn((M, K), dtype=torch.float16)
b = torch.randn((K, N), dtype=torch.float16)
ref = torch.matmul(a, b)        # high‑precision reference (torch uses fp32 accumulation)
out = matmul(a, b)              # Triton kernel under test
# The original kernel (fp32 accumulator) should meet the 0.125 absolute tolerance,
# whereas the mutant (fp16 accumulator) will exceed it due to reduced‑precision accumulation.
assert torch.allclose(out, ref, atol=0.125, rtol=0), \
    f"Accumulator precision test failed for shape ({M},{N},{K})"
